Provides clear guidance on managing post-treatment photosensitivity, expected purging, and bacterial rebalancing. Strong emphasis on gentle antibacterial care without compromising the skin barrier. Realistic expectations about treatment series and maintenance.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare protocol is for light-based treatments specifically targeting Propionibacterium acnes bacteria (e.g., blue light, photodynamic therapy). The treatment creates reactive oxygen species that destroy acne-causing bacteria. Care focuses on supporting the skin's microbiome while managing inflammation and preventing rebound.

instructions.general_directive: Follow this guidance for 7-10 days. The treatment has made your skin photosensitive and altered its bacterial balance; gentle care is essential.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Response
sections.content: Your skin will be red, may feel warm or tingly, and could appear slightly swollen. This inflammatory response indicates bacterial destruction. Existing inflamed pimples may temporarily look darker or flatter.

sections.title: Critical: Photosensitivity Management
sections.content: The treatment makes your skin EXTREMELY sensitive to light for 24-48 hours. You must avoid ALL direct sunlight and bright indoor lights. Wear a wide-brimmed hat and stay indoors as much as possible. This sensitivity is temporary but critical to prevent burns.

sections.title: Healing Timeline & Bacterial Rebalancing
items: Days 1-3: Skin is sensitive, red, and may feel dry. Use only gentle, non-antibacterial cleansers to allow natural flora to re-establish.
Days 3-7: A mild 'purge' of existing microcomedones is common as inflammation resolves. Redness subsides. You may reintroduce gentle acne treatments.
Weeks 2-4: Bacterial balance normalizes. Active acne lesions should be significantly reduced.

sections.title: Skincare for Post-Antibacterial Treatment
items: Days 1-3: Use only gentle, pH-balanced cleansers without harsh antibacterials (avoid benzoyl peroxide, harsh sulfates).
Day 4+: Gradually reintroduce antibacterial products at HALF strength to avoid resistance. Consider alternating days with gentle products.
Moisturize with non-comedogenic, barrier-supporting products containing ceramides or niacinamide.
Avoid topical antibiotics unless prescribed, as they can disrupt the newly balanced microbiome.

sections.title: Sun Protection (Non-Negotiable)
sections.content: Even after photosensitivity subsides, apply oil-free SPF 30+ daily. UV exposure can reactivate inflammation and bacteria.

sections.title: Activity Restrictions
items: Avoid sweating and exercise for 48 hours to prevent bacterial overgrowth in moist environments.
Avoid swimming in chlorinated water for 72 hours.
Change pillowcases and face towels frequently during first week.

sections.title: Results & Treatment Series
sections.content: Bacterial reduction is not permanent. A series of 4-8 treatments spaced 1-2 weeks apart is typical for significant reduction. Maintenance treatments every 4-8 weeks may be needed. Follow-up at 2 weeks to assess bacterial response.

patient_declaration.reading_confirmation: Targeting acne bacteria requires careful rebalancing of your skin's ecosystem. Please follow this guidance.
patient_declaration.question_opportunity: Ask about probiotic skincare options to support healthy bacterial balance post-treatment.
patient_declaration.declaration_text: I understand the photosensitivity risks and bacterial rebalancing process after my acne bacteria reduction treatment.
